name: Dave Thompson
office: Council (City of Victoria) — and CRD Board, same ballot, 17 Oct 2026

doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: "The overall tax increase is 7.28%." · "5.06 percentage points (about 70% of the entire increase) is attributable to the police budget increases." He supported the 2026 financial plan; the three recorded opponents were Kim, Hammond and Gardiner. He explains the bill. He proposes no cap, and no residential-rate number.

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "The Police and City Bylaw Services will be more present on the street." · "a Police and Bylaw field hub will soon be opening in the Neighbour Building at 999 Pandora" · "city council funded the additional police foot patrols". Reported as news, not proposed as policy — no bylaw hours, no unified command, no Public Order Team. He is not individually named on the foot-patrol funding.

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "I'm committed to doing so" — approving more multifamily homes. At OCP adoption: "We will allow a wider variety of homes, and yes corner stores, in more neighbourhoods." No unit target and no composition share.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: Authorized 2026 site, current, with a dated blog. "I'm standing for re-election to Victoria City Council and the CRD Board on October 17, and I'm putting together my platform." Six preliminary priority areas, explicitly consultative. Written and current; no costed platform, no targets, no dates.

cells.quote: Commits + neither. 18 Mar 2026: committed to approving more multifamily homes — "I'm committed to doing so". Volume without a unit target and without a composition share, so none of M6's instrument (12,000 homes; 25% missing middle; 20% 3BR+; 15% below-market; 30% PBR, quarterly reported). The 4% vacancy discussion in that post is analysis, not a City target. 📋 Record YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023, named — matches, not in n.
Commits + comparable instrument. OCP adoption, 12 May 2026: "We will allow a wider variety of homes, and yes corner stores, in more neighbourhoods.
cells.why: "We are going to go back to allowing homeowners a wider range of choices on what to do with their property." City-wide land-use liberalisation is comparable to M8's pre-zoning leg, but it is not the same instrument: no 5% vacancy target, no DCC reduction for purpose-built rental, no suite amnesty. 📋 Record, matching, not in n: he moved a motion with Coun. Loughton directing staff to examine house conversions, eliminating parking minimums and multiple suites on a single property — carried 6–3.

cells.quote: a Police and Bylaw field hub will soon be opening in the Neighbour Building at 999 Pandora
cells.why: "city council funded the additional police foot patrols". A co-located police-and-bylaw hub is adjacent to M26's co-located operations desk, but he reports it, he does not propose it — no unified command, no 8 AM briefing, no single field supervisor, no Public Works or outreach leg. He is not individually named on the funding vote. Shown, not scored.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)

cells.quote: Agrees + neither. "Bringing people indoors means they can stabilize, and more easily access and be accessed by providers of services, such as detox and addiction treatment." That is M35's capacity-first principle, and he enumerates the capacity coming online (Pathways 34, Rock Bay 30, Johnson Manor 20, Salvation Army ARC 13, Village on the Green 32, 926–930 Pandora 47). He names no instrument in this topic: no rapid-removal protocol, no 5 PM capacity dashboard, no reclaiming-spaces deployment, no all-night lighting.

cells.what: tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: Supported the 2026 financial plan; the recorded opponents were Kim, Hammond and Gardiner. His 4 Jun post explains the number — "The overall tax increase is 7.28%." and "5.06 percentage points (about 70% of the entire increase) is attributable to the police budget increases" — the same arithmetic the Program uses. Explaining a bill is not capping one: no residential-rate cap, no glide path, no supermajority override.
cells.why: No 2026 promise is contradicted, so shown and not in n.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.why: OCP adoption, 12 May 2026: "This was a motion to add a tangible, aspirational goal of building 1,500 hotel rooms by 2035." A named, dated sector target, adopted in his own remarks. No instrument: no storefront-vacancy target, no vacant-property licensing, no Strategic Economic Plan, no single mandate. Authorship of the motion is not established — if he moved it this rises to Partial+ 1.5. Scored conservatively.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: Commits + same instrument. "This week, Councillors Caradonna, Dell, and I will bring a motion that would be the first step toward requiring landlords to allow and/or provide cooling in Victoria's rental buildings.
cells.why: "Our motion asks staff to look at what tools the City has to restrict landlords from blocking cooling equipment, or to require heat pumps or other passive cooling measures." That is M64's step 1 word for word — ban unreasonable landlord prohibition of portable cooling, carried by the Standards of Maintenance Bylaw or the business-licence power. The motion also asks staff to write to the Province so upgrades do not trigger renovictions, which touches M9. Only the 26°C performance rule and the enforcement FTE are gated in the Program; step 1 is not.

cells.quote: Commits + comparable instrument. "I brought a motion to help people get into the Detox-Treatment-Recovery System.
cells.why: "A Detox-Treatment-Recovery System Access Navigator could proactively approach people on the streets." · "This would not be a wide-ranging social worker or health-care worker, but rather a person whose only job is to reach out to people and help them contact appropriate offices." A named, targeted throughput role — comparable to M11's case-managed STEP pathway, but on the treatment system rather than the housing ladder, with no 50% unsheltered target and no published cost-per-placement.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
cells.why: "I was very happy to move a successful Victoria Council motion calling on the provincial government to: create the Student Food Security Grant called for in the Backgrounder; set a $10 flat-rate ferry fare for students foot passengers; and explore and consult with student advocacy organizations in relation to all 15 of the recommendations made in the Backgrounder." The fare leg and the student-consultation leg are comparable to M13c's fare partnership and Youth Voice, delivered as provincial advocacy rather than a City instrument. Nothing on childcare spaces (M12) or family doctors (M13b).

cells.what: mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: Commits + same instrument, twice. Cameras (M40 as rewritten to advocacy): "I made a motion in 2023 at Committee of the Whole" asking the Province to install safety cameras at high-crash locations or permit municipalities to do so at their own expense
cells.why: "This motion passed unanimously at Committee and Council" · "I gave notice of a similar motion at the CRD Transportation Committee" · "The next steps rest with the Provincial Government." Protected lanes (M41): he and Coun. Dell brought a motion to fill two network gaps, and his 2024 Shelbourne motion carried unanimously. Caveat: M19 adaptive signals is unmatched — the mark rests on M40 and M41, both of which remain in the Program. Downgrade to Close 2.0 if you want the flagship instrument to govern the cluster.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls
VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: Council cut VicPD's four-officer ask to two on 3 Mar 2026, carried 5–4; the four opponents are named (Coleman, Gardiner, Hammond, Alto), so on a nine-member council he is in the majority by exclusion, not by a named roll-call. The board appealed on 16 Jun 2026. His own 2026 position points a different way from the Program: "I'd love to see it changed to eliminate council's middleman role" — that is not M29's renegotiated cost-share formula and not M29b's convened regional review.
cells.why: No 2026 promise of his is contradicted, so this is shown and not scored.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target
culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging

cells.quote: Agrees + neither. "Having new growth occur in existing urban areas is the most powerful tool that local governments have to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions that cause climate change.
cells.why: "we need more of our growth to take place in the right places". The goal is named and argued with data (30% of growth transit-served 2012–15, 16% in the last five years), but the instrument is land use, not M58's target reaffirmation and annual progress publication — and nothing on district energy or seismic. The 30%/16% figures are diagnosis, not targets he adopts.

cells.what: trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness
cells.quote: Agrees + neither. "It is not 'trees vs housing;' its trees and housing.
cells.why: "Victoria has added over 100 soccer fields worth of tree canopy while adding 8,000 net new homes, almost all of them multifamily apartment or condo." Canopy is named as a goal to hold alongside supply, with no planting number, no canopy percentage, no date and no instrument. The 25 Aug "more street trees and tree canopy" bullet is a preliminary Mention and cannot lift this.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
cells.quote: Named NO on the non-binding ballot question, 25 Jun 2026: "It was a narrow 5-4 vote with Couns.
cells.why: Jeremy Caradonna, Stephen Hammond, Marg Gardiner and Dave Thompson opposed." Not Opposed on the Program: M81 says finish the file and do not re-run the process, so a vote against another non-binding question does not contradict it. He publishes no 2026 amalgamation position of his own. Shown, not scored.
